alignments.note: Imperative הַלְלוּ rendered with the volitive frame 'Oh praise'; rule 17 puts the framing 'Oh' in the verb's unit, headed on the lexical verb.
Object marker אֵת with the object rendered bare ('praise Jehovah'); rule 16.
Construct כֹּל takes only its own 'all'; rule 19.

Vocative noun takes the supplied 'ye' written immediately before it (rule 36; cf. 'all ye stars of light'). The 'ye' stands before the noun, not after the imperative, so it is the noun's rather than the verb's.
Article on a vocative; the ASV writes no 'the' and the vocative 'ye' belongs to the noun, not the article (rule 36).
Vocative noun takes the supplied 'ye' standing before it; rule 36.

review_notes: Both cola: 'all ye X' — 'ye' assigned to the vocative noun by position (rule 36), כֹּל keeps 'all' only, imperatives keep only their own verb (plus the volitive 'Oh' on the first).

alignments.note: Finite גָּבַר rendered 'is great' — copula plus adjective complement; rule 44 heads on the complement carrying the lexeme.
Construct noun with no article morpheme takes the supplied 'the'; rule 29.

Prepositional predicate of a verbless clause: rule 49 gives the supplied linking verb 'endureth' to the לְ together with its own 'for' (the contract's own example לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ → 'endureth for ever'), headed on the written preposition. The ASV italic on 'endureth' corroborates the supply and decides nothing (rule 7); the competing reading marks 'endureth' added under rule 20, but continuance through the stated time is what a copula asserts here.
Imperative takes its supplied subject pronoun 'ye'; rule 17. No vocative stands in this clause to compete for it.
Short divine name יָהּ → 'Jehovah'. The margin's 'Hebrew Hallelujah' was read and set aside; the printed text governs (rule 38).

review_notes: 'endureth for ever' placed on the predicate לְ under rule 49's resultative/continuance reading, matching the contract's לְעוֹלָם חַסְדּוֹ example; the 'endureth' is the construction's linking verb, not a supplied lexical one.
גָּבַר → 'is great' treated as a single verb unit headed on 'great' (rule 44).
